arxiv-2106-05161.title: Interactive Modelling of Volumetric Musculoskeletal Anatomy Price: 15.00 Journal: TOG Volume: 40 4 122 8 DOI: 10.1145/3450626.3459769 CCS: Computing methodologies Mesh geometry models CCS: Computing methodologies Volumetric models CCS: Computing methodologies Graphics systems and interfaces
arxiv-2106-05161.creator: Rinat Abdrashitov, Seungbae Bang, David Levin, Karan Singh, Alec Jacobson
arxiv-2106-05161.description: Abstract . We present a new approach for modelling musculoskeletal anatomy. Unlike previous methods, we do not model individual muscle shapes as geometric primitives (polygonal meshes, NURBS etc.). Instead, we adopt a volumetric segmentation approach where every point in our volume is assigned to a muscle, fat, or bone tissue.

arxiv-2301-12502.title: First-principles calculation of the frequency-dependent dipole polarizability of argon
arxiv-2301-12502.creator: Michał Lesiuk, Bogumił Jeziorski
arxiv-2301-12502.description: Abstract In this work we report state-of-the-art theoretical calculations of the dipole polarizability of the argon atom. Frequency dependence of the polarizability is taken into account by means of the dispersion coefficients (Cauchy coefficients) which is sufficient for experimentally relevant wavelengths below the first resonant frequency.

arxiv-2401-06409.creator: Dmitry Valentinovich Agafonov, Arina Romanovna Kuznetsova, Mikhail Evgenievich Kompan, Vladislav Gennadievich Malyshkin
arxiv-2401-06409.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Dmitry Valentinovich Agafonov, Arina Romanovna Kuznetsova, Mikhail Evgenievich Kompan, Vladislav Gennadievich Malyshkin. $Id: timedomain.tex,v 1.399 2024/02/11 10:19:40 mal Exp $ A novel time-domain technique for supercapacitor characterization is developed, modeled numerically, and experimentally tested on a number of commercial supercapacitors.

arxiv-2406-01649.title: CoLa-DCE – Concept-guided Latent Diffusion Counterfactual Explanations
arxiv-2406-01649.creator: Franz Motzkus, Christian Hellert, Ute Schmid
arxiv-2406-01649.description: Abstract Recent advancements in generative AI have introduced novel prospects and practical implementations. Especially diffusion models show their strength in generating diverse and, at the same time, realistic features, positioning them well for generating counterfactual explanations for computer vision models.

arxiv-2406-08970.title: Stabilization of a twisted modulus on a mirror of rigid Calabi-Yau manifold
arxiv-2406-08970.creator: Keiya Ishiguro 1, Takafumi Kai 2 , and, Hajime Otsuka 2
arxiv-2406-08970.description: Abstract We study the stabilization of a twisted modulus in Type IIB flux compactifications on a mirror of the rigid Calabi-Yau threefold. By analyzing the effective action of twisted and untwisted moduli, we find that three-form fluxes satisfying the tadpole cancellation conditions lead to supersymmetric AdS vacua. We also investigate swampland conjectures on this non-geometric background.

arxiv-2502-15577.creator: Clement Ruah, Houssem Sifaou, Osvaldo Simeone, and Bashir Al-Hashimi
arxiv-2502-15577.description: Abstract The widespread adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in next-generation communication systems is challenged by the heterogeneity of traffic and network conditions, which call for the use of highly contextual, site-specific, data. A promising solution is to rely not only on real-world data, but also on synthetic pseudo-data generated by a network digital twin (NDT) .

arxiv-2601-12705.title: How do the Global South Diasporas Mobilize for Transnational Political Change? Conference: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems; April 13–17, 2026; Barcelona, Spain Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI ’26), April 1
arxiv-2601-12705.creator: Dipto Das, Afrin Prio, Pritu Saha, Shion Guha, Syed Ishtiaque Ahmed
arxiv-2601-12705.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Dipto Das, Afrin Prio, Pritu Saha, Shion Guha, Syed Ishtiaque Ahmed. This paper examines how non-resident Bangladeshis mobilized during the 2024 quota-reform turned pro-democracy movement, leveraging social platforms and remittance flows to challenge state authority. Drawing on semi-structured interviews, we identify four phases of their collective action: technology-mediated shifts to active engagement, rapid transnational network building, strategic execution of remittance boycott, reframing economic dependence as political leverage, and adaptive responses to government surveillance and information blackouts.

pmc-10559285.title: Exploring novel strategies to improve anti-tumour efficiency: The potential for targeting reactive oxygen species
pmc-10559285.creator: Rumbidzai Sharon Chasara, Taiwo Oreoluwa Ajayi, Dineo Motjoadi Leshilo, Madan Sai Poka, Bwalya Angel Witika
pmc-10559285.description: The cellular milieu in which malignant growths or cancer stem cells reside is known as the tumour microenvironment (TME). It is the consequence of the interactivity amongst malignant and non-malignant cells and directly affects cancer development and progression. Reactive oxygen species (ROS) are chemically reactive molecules that contain oxygen, they are generated because of numerous endogenous and external factors.

pmc-11314582.title: New Ethylated Derivatives of Sulfur- and Nitrogen-Containing Artifacts from Tenodera sinensis Egg Pod and Their Anti-Renal Fibrosis
pmc-11314582.creator: Ye-Fei Chen, Shi-Gang Peng, Yong-Ming Yan, Yong-Xian Cheng
pmc-11314582.description: Three pairs of enantiomers and one achiral molecule that are new ethylated derivatives of sulfur and nitrogen-containing compounds named mantidisamides E–H (1–4), along with twenty known ones (5–24), were derived from the ethanol extract of Tenodera sinensis Saussure. The structures of these new compounds and their absolute configurations were assigned on the basis of spectroscopic analyses and computational methods.

pmc-11416246.title: A tailless FBG smart bolt with good performance
pmc-11416246.creator: Dan Hou, Min Zheng, Zhimin Yang, Run Li, Xiaojin Li
pmc-11416246.description: A novel type of tailless FBG smart bolt with good performance is developed. Owe to the innovative design of an integrated FBG sensor comprising a strain measured FBG and a temperature-compensated FBG, the tailless FBG smart bolt serves the purpose of torque monitoring or bolt looseness monitoring.

pmc-12470308.title: Distribution of Larval Habitats and Efficiency of Various Trap Settings to Monitor Sympatric Aedes albopictus and Aedes aegypti in La Reunion
pmc-12470308.creator: Caroline Vitry, Ronan Brouazin, Anthony Herbin, Mathieu Whiteside, Cécile Brengues, Thierry Baldet, Renaud Lancelot, Jérémy Bouyer, Athanasios Giatropoulos
pmc-12470308.description: Simple SummaryTwo Aedes mosquitoes, vectors of dengue and chikungunya viruses, are found in Saint-Joseph (La Reunion): Aedes albopictus (the most widespread and abundant) and Aedes aegypti, with contrasted ecology. This study aimed to prepare for a boosted sterile insect technique control trial using sterile male Aedes albopictus treated with a larval biocide.

pmc-12747365.title: Towards responsible surveillance in preventive health data-AI research
pmc-12747365.creator: Sam H. A. Muller, Johannes J. M. van Delden, Ghislaine J. M. W. van Thiel, Hypermarker Consortium, Po-Chih Kuo, Po-Chih Kuo
pmc-12747365.description: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into health data research promises to transform precision medicine, especially by managing complex and chronic conditions like hypertension through decision support. Yet health AI also furthers surveillance, with serious ethical and social impact. Nevertheless, surveillance in health, in particular data-AI research and innovation, is understudied.

pmc-12983222.title: A new indoloquinoline-based fluorescence probe for imaging of hydrazine in vitro and in vivo
pmc-12983222.creator: Caiju Zhang, Shi Tang, Jianyong Wu, Wenxing Lv, Junjian Li, Chu Tang
pmc-12983222.description: The detection of hydrazine is critically important due to its potential to cause severe damage to ecosystems. Herein, a novel indoloquinoline-based “turn-off” fluorescent probe was specifically devised and fabricated for the detection of hydrazine. The probe demonstrates excellent qualities including rapid response, high sensitivity, excellent selectivity, and low cytotoxicity in vitro.

pmc-13392010.title: A systematic review examining the association between parity and gravidity & hypertension and blood pressure
pmc-13392010.creator: Nabilah Gulamhusein, Badal S. B. Pattar, Sandra M. Dumanski, Tyrone G. Harrison, Sonia Butalia, Magali Robert, Jane Schulz, Sofia B. Ahmed
pmc-13392010.description: Parity and gravidity have been shown to be associated with hypertension and changes in blood pressure, but results are conflicting. We aimed to estimate the association between gravidity and parity with hypertension and blood pressure. A systematic search of multiple databases was performed. Studies were included if they reported on parity or gravidity and hypertension or blood pressure.

pmc-13414022.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of p16 Immunohistochemistry as a Marker of High-Risk HPV in Invasive Laryngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Systematic Review
pmc-13414022.creator: Ana-Maria Stanoiu, Delia Hutanu, Maria Sorop-Florea, Alexandru Alexandru, Norberth-Istvan Varga, Iulia Cristina Bagiu, Mihaela-Diana Popa, Bogdan Hirtie, Nicolae-Constantin Balica, Cristian-Ion Mot, Ioana-Delia Horhat
pmc-13414022.description: Background and Objectives: p16 immunohistochemistry (IHC) is widely used as a surrogate marker for high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV)-driven carcinogenesis in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma. Diagnostic reliability in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) is still up for debate, particularly because HPV DNA detection, p16 overexpression, and transcriptionally active HPV infection may be discordant at this anatomical site.

pmc-13532340.title: Dental wastewater reveals a hidden reservoir of oral bacteriophage diversity
pmc-13532340.creator: Carli Roush, Marvin Whiteley
pmc-13532340.description: Bacteriophages (phages) are being explored as alternatives or complements to antibiotics because of their ability to selectively kill bacterial pathogens. However, phages that infect many oral bacteria remain undiscovered. Here, we discovered that dental wastewater harbors previously underexplored phage diversity. Viral particles concentrated from dental wastewater displayed diverse morphologies, including abundant filamentous phage-like particles.
